selection: Four authentic specimen photographs for granite, diorite, basalt and sandstone. All four are individually verified CC0; originals visually inspected before optimization.
limitations: These four photographs show museum/collection specimens, not documented river finds.
No reliable reusable rounded river-worn examples were selected in this pass; no before-and-after relationship is implied.
Diorite roadcut photograph from the NPS igneous guide was considered and rejected as too distant to show identification texture clearly.
Granite specimen color is not representative of all granite; no additional gray/pink comparison photograph was selected in this pass.

images.identity: Diorite, near Azusa, California; Ward’s Collection of Classic North American Rocks #25; GeoDIL image35
images.credit: Joseph Hartman / Geoscience Digital Image Library
images.collectionContext: Photographed hand specimen, 10cm across according to source; not documented as a river find.
images.caption: Diorite hand specimen from near Azusa, California. Pale plagioclase and dark hornblende make the medium-grained speckled texture; the source identifies the specimen as 10 cm across.
images.alt: Diorite hand specimen showing strongly contrasting pale mineral grains and black hornblende against a black background.
images.licenseEvidence: Exact image page HTML contains a copyright row linking CC0 1.0 with zero.svg license icon. GeoDIL copyright page warns not all images are freely licensed, so this image-specific license was checked; Commons independently records CC0 and source review on18August2026.
images.visualReview: Original downloaded photograph inspected with view_image. Full single angular black-and-pale crystalline hand specimen clearly visible on black background; distinct interlocking grains and dark hornblende are visible. No generative edits or cropping; no river origin inferred.
images.optimization: Full frame preserved; resized without enlargement to1400px and560px widths; JPEG quality90 with4:4:4chroma. No AI or color alterations.

images.caption: Basalt from the Smithsonian teaching collection, Hawaii. Look for the dark, fine-grained material and cavities; many basalts are more compact than this example.
images.alt: Dark basalt teaching specimen with a fine-grained surface, ropy upper surface and visible cavities beside a centimeter scale.
